a: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS/SSL. It encrypts data between browser and server so it cannot be read in transit.
TLS (formerly SSL) is the protocol that encrypts HTTPS connections and verifies server identity with certificates.
A firewall filters network traffic by rules to allow or block connections.
A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel between your device and a remote server so traffic is private on public networks.
DNS translates domain names (example.com) into IP addresses computers use to connect.
An IP address identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1 or 2001:db8::1).
A load balancer spreads traffic across multiple servers so no single server is overloaded.
A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users to make sites faster and more reliable.
Rate limiting restricts how many requests a client can make in a time window to prevent abuse.
SQL injection is an attack where untrusted input is executed as SQL. Prevent it with parameterized queries.
XSS (cross-site scripting) injects malicious scripts into web pages. Escape output and use Content-Security-Policy.
CSRF tricks a logged-in browser into sending unwanted requests. Mitigate with CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies.
Hashing maps data to a fixed-size digest. Same input → same hash. Used for passwords and integrity checks.
Encryption transforms data so only someone with the key can read it. Symmetric uses one key; asymmetric uses a key pair.
Microservices split an app into small independent services that communicate over the network (often HTTP/gRPC).
A monolith is a single deployable application where most features live in one codebase and process.
A cache stores frequently used data in fast storage (memory) to avoid repeated expensive work.
Redis is an in-memory data store often used as a cache, queue, or session store.
PostgreSQL is a powerful open-source relational database with strong SQL support and reliability.
MongoDB is a document database that stores JSON-like documents instead of rigid tables.
A message queue (e.g. RabbitMQ, Kafka) lets services send work asynchronously so producers and consumers scale independently.
An idempotent operation can be repeated safely with the same result (important for retries in APIs).
REST exposes fixed endpoints and resources. GraphQL lets the client request exactly the fields it needs in one query.
Horizontal scaling means adding more machines. Vertical scaling means giving one machine more CPU/RAM.
